title: Best 50-Pint Dehumidifier (2026): Midea, Frigidaire & More
dek: The workhorse size for basements and big rooms — as long as the "50" on the box means 50 under today's test.
description: The best 50-pint dehumidifier for 2026, ranked by real DOE capacity: Midea, Frigidaire, hOmeLabs and the one Honeywell that's truly 50 pints.
intro: A 50-pint dehumidifier is the size most households end up needing. It's big enough to keep a damp basement, a garage or a large open living area in check, yet still rolls around on casters and plugs into an ordinary outlet. It's the top of the residential range before you step into ducted or commercial equipment.

The trouble is that "50-pint" isn't as fixed a number as it sounds. In 2019 the Department of Energy changed how dehumidifiers are tested, and every rating shifted downward. Some brands still put old-scale numbers in their model names, so a unit called "50" might be rated far lower today — and one called "70" might be the true 50-pinter. We sorted that out so you can shop on real capacity.

Our picks come from DOE 2019 ratings, manufacturer spec sheets and manuals, ENERGY STAR listings, discontinuation notices and recurring patterns in owner reviews. We don't lab-test; when we cite a figure, it's a published rating.
topPicksLead: The **Midea Cube 50** is the 50-pint unit we'd buy first: real DOE 2019 capacity, low published power draw and an oversized reservoir that cuts down on emptying.

If you'd like the same design with a pump or in a smaller size, see our [best Midea dehumidifier](/best/best-midea-dehumidifier/) guide.

items.label: How much lower pint ratings run under the DOE's 2019 test than the old one
Typical rated coverage for a true 50-pint unit in a damp space
Actual DOE 2019 rating of Honeywell's TPFIT50AWK, despite its name

blocks.text: The first number explains the third. When the DOE dropped the test temperature from 80°F to 65°F, less water condensed out of the test air, so every machine's rating fell. Today's 50-pint unit is roughly what would have been sold as a 70-pinter before 2019.

We started by confirming each model's capacity under the current DOE 2019 procedure, ignoring the number in the model name. From there we compared manufacturer spec sheets for wattage and amperage, drainage options and rated coverage, and checked ENERGY STAR listings and the CPSC recall database.

We also checked brand product pages for discontinuation notices — which is how the GE APYR50LC dropped off our list in favor of GE's current APER50LZ pump model — and read owner reviews for recurring issues like failed pumps, leaking buckets and inaccurate humidity readouts. We don't run our own tests.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 50-pint dehumidifier

items.label: A DOE 2019 rating on the spec sheet
items.text: Trust the current rating, not the model number. Honeywell's lineup is the clearest example of names still tied to the old scale.

items.label: The right drainage for your space
items.text: No floor drain? Get a pump. A floor drain within reach? A gravity hose is simpler and has fewer parts to fail. Compare options in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

items.label: Reservoir size, if you'll use the bucket
items.text: A larger tank, like the Cube 50's, can mean emptying every couple of days instead of twice a day in peak season.

items.label: Power draw
items.text: Among today's top 50-pint picks, wattage is close enough that it shouldn't decide the purchase. Pick on drainage, tank size or price.

items.label: Coverage matched to dampness
items.text: A musty basement and a basement with seepage need different capacity even at the same square footage. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) breaks it down.

blocks.text: Nearly every major appliance brand sells a 50-pint model, and many shoppers start their search with a brand name. Here's where the other popular options fit.

If you like the Frigidaire but don't have a floor drain, the brand's pump-equipped 50-pinter (such as the FFAP5033W1) pushes water up to a sink or window instead of filling a bucket. It's the natural step up from our value pick; compare it with other self-draining units in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.

TCL's Wi-Fi 50-pinter is a frequent value alternative to the bigger names. Confirm the DOE 2019 rating and drainage options on the exact model before you buy; our [best TCL dehumidifier](/best/best-tcl-dehumidifier/) guide covers the lineup.

With the APYR50LC discontinued, the APER50LZ above is GE's current pump model, and the rest of GE's 50-pint lineup is covered in our [best GE dehumidifier](/best/best-ge-dehumidifier/) guide. Hisense sells 50-pint units with and without a pump; read our [best Hisense dehumidifier](/best/best-hisense-dehumidifier/) guide first, since owner reports raise a reliability caveat on the pump version.

sections.heading: Is a 50-pint dehumidifier the right size?

blocks.text: For most residential basements in the 2,500 to 4,500 square-foot range with typical dampness — a musty smell, occasional condensation on pipes or windows — a 50-pint unit is the sweet spot. It cycles on and off to hold your target instead of running nonstop, which is easier on both the compressor and your electric bill.

items: **Size down** to a [30-pint dehumidifier](/best/best-30-pint-dehumidifier/) if you're treating a single room closer to 1,500 square feet.
**Size up** to a [70-pint unit](/best/best-70-pint-dehumidifier/) or commercial equipment if you have standing water, active seepage or a very large open footprint.

**Consider two units** in a long, chopped-up basement where one machine can't move air into every corner. Our [2,000 sq ft guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-2000-sq-ft/) covers when that makes sense.

blocks.title: Set it and check it
blocks.text: Aim the humidistat at 45–50% and confirm with a standalone hygrometer for the first few weeks. Built-in sensors can read several points off.

The **Midea Cube 50** is the best 50-pint dehumidifier for most homes, thanks to its true DOE 2019 capacity, modest power draw and oversized reservoir. Choose the **hOmeLabs HME031004N** if you have no floor drain and want a pump, the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** if price leads the decision, the **GE APER50LZ** for a pump model from GE, and the **Honeywell TP70PWKN** if you prefer Honeywell — just not the confusingly named TPFIT50AWK. For basement-specific picks, see our [best dehumidifier for basement](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/) guide.

faqs.a: The Midea Cube 50 (MAD50S1QWT). It's rated at a true 50 pints a day under the DOE 2019 test, covers up to about 4,500 square feet, draws roughly 512 watts in published measurements and has a 34-pint reservoir that needs emptying far less often than a standard bucket.

faqs.q: Is the Frigidaire 50-pint dehumidifier with Wi-Fi worth it?
faqs.a: For most buyers, yes. The FHDD5034Y1 is a genuine 50-pint unit under the DOE 2019 test, adds Wi-Fi and Alexa control, restarts automatically after a power outage, and its listed 470-watt draw is close to the Midea Cube 50's. You give up the Cube's oversized reservoir, not capacity.

faqs.q: What does "50-pint" mean under the current DOE rating?
faqs.a: In 2019 the DOE lowered the test temperature from 80°F to 65°F. Cooler air gives up less water, so ratings dropped about 30%. A unit sold as 50-pint today performs roughly like a pre-2019 70-pint model — same hardware, stricter test.

faqs.q: How large a space can a 50-pint dehumidifier handle?
faqs.a: Most true 50-pint units are rated for about 4,500 square feet in a moderately damp space, and a few, like the hOmeLabs HME031004N, list 7,000 square feet or more. How wet the space is matters as much as its size.

faqs.q: Is the Honeywell 50-pint dehumidifier really 50 pints?
faqs.a: It depends on the model. Honeywell's TPFIT50AWK has "50" in its name but is rated at just 32 pints under the current DOE standard. Its genuine 50-pinters are the TP70PWKN and the Wi-Fi TP70AWKNR, whose names still reference the old pre-2019 scale. Always read the DOE 2019 rating on the spec sheet.

faqs.q: Is a 50-pint dehumidifier enough for a whole basement?
faqs.a: For most basements up to roughly 2,500–4,500 square feet with ordinary dampness, yes. If there's standing water, active seepage or a much larger area, step up to a 70-pint or commercial unit, or run two machines.

faqs.q: Should I get the Frigidaire 50-pint dehumidifier with a built-in pump?
faqs.a: Only if there's no floor drain within reach of a gravity hose and you don't want to empty a bucket. The pump version pushes water up and out to a sink or window, which is especially handy in below-grade basements. If a drain is nearby, the standard FHDD5034Y1 with a gravity hose is simpler and usually costs less.
